newsitem.title: CHINA: RIVER IN DROUGHT-HIT CHINA PROVINCE FLOWS AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: RIVER IN DROUGHT-HIT CHINA PROVINCE FLOWS AGAIN.

text.p: Water has begun to flow again in a stretch of the Yellow River in China's eastern Shandong province after rains eased a severe drought that left the river dry for 132 days, the China Daily said on Thursday.

Water from the river's upper reaches flowed into the Bohai gulf on Wednesday, passing through the Lijin Hydrometric station at 510 cubic metres per second, it quoted Kong Guofeng of the Shandong Yellow River Administration as saying.
The water was expected to help to ease the effects of drought in western parts of the province, the newspaper said.
The drought had affected more than 3.7 million hectares of farmland in Shandong and direct economic losses were expected to exceed 6.0 billion yuan ($723 million), it said.

Recent rainfall was expected to relieve water shortages in southern parts of the province but the drought in northwestern Shandong and the province's Jiaodong peninsula remained severe, it quoted local water conservancy officials as saying.
Stretches of the Yellow River, the main water source for western and northern Shandong, ran dry in February after severe drought struck its upper and middle reaches, the China Daily said.

The river has dried up 19 times in the last 25 years, costing local industry and agriculture a total of 26.8 billion yuan, and experts had warned the dry spells were getting longer each year, it said.

Unseasonably high temperatures and low rainfall across northern and northeastern China have affected a record 20 million hectares of crops and farmland, threatening the autumn grain crop, state media has said.

Officials have said the drought is expected to cut the size of China's corn harvest this year, although overall grain production is expected to be about 484 million tonnes, only slightly below last year's record 490 million tonnes.
While drought and high temperatures have been plaguing northern China, floods have wreaked havoc in the south.
